newsitem.title: USA: N.J. judge to rule next week on Trump tunnel suit.
newsitem.headline: N.J. judge to rule next week on Trump tunnel suit.

text.p: A New Jersey judge Friday said he would rule within a week on casino magnate Donald Trump's challenge to the financing terms of a highway project that would serve a potential rival.

Lawyers for Trump argued that using revenues of the Casino Reinvestment Development Authority to help pay for the viaduct -- instead of for housing the poor or senior citizens or the disabled -- violates the 1976 amendment to the state constitution that legalized casino gaming here.
The CRDA sought a ruling from Superior Court Judge Richard Williams so it could proceed with a bond issue. The agency has agreed to pay a $65-million share of the project's $330-million cost.
Stephen Wynn, CEO of Mirage Resorts Inc, called the connector to the Atlantic City Expressway a precondition for his project. Mirage and the state agreed Sept. 18 on a public-private partnership.
Trump, who owns three hotel-casinos in Atlantic City through his Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc, has been a vociferous opponent of the plan.

Mirage plans a $750-million, 2,000-room hotel-casino to be called Beau Rivage, surrounded by retail and entertainment facilities. Wynn has also brought in two co-developers -- Circus Circus Enterprises and Boyd Gaming Corp. Each has announced plans for a casino-hotel of similar scale, although neither has applied for regulatory approval.
Lawyers for the state argued that the law was changed in 1993 to give the CRDA a wider range of investments -- including spurring more hotel construction and a new convention center.
Judge Williams said his ruling should come Wednesday.
A federal suit Trump filed was dismissed on the grounds it raised issues for a state court.
